chapter.name: Parallel and Intersecting Lines
chapter.names_note: Names are {{NAME_n}} placeholders from name_slots.json (one character, one token, chapter-wide); a named person takes no gendered pronoun.

source: Creases on a folded paper
videos.handover: Try it: fold a sheet of paper a few times, draw a pencil line along two creases, and decide whether they would meet if you drew them much longer. Keep your answer for the next topic.
videos.note: The hook leaves the folded-paper question open. Do not say that any pair meets or does not meet; the words intersect and parallel are settled in the next topics.

source: Farhan draws two lines that cross and measures the four angl

items.question: Farhan draws two lines that cross and measures the four angles with a protractor, going round the point: a = 63°, b = 117°, c = 63° and d = 117°. What pattern do the four angles show?
steps: Neighbouring angles: 63 + 117 = 180, and 117 + 63 = 180.
Angles that face each other: a and c are both 63°, and b and d are both 117°.
So neighbouring angles add to 180° and facing angles are equal, in this pair of lines.
Two straight lines meet at one point only, so there are exactly four angles at the crossing.
items.answer: Neighbours add to 180° and facing angles are equal; two straight lines meet at one point only

videos.answer: Neighbours add to 180° and facing angles are equal; two straight lines meet at one point only

source: Two lines cross. The angle a is 120°. Find b, c and d going

items.question: Two lines cross. The angle a is 120°. Find b, c and d going round the point, without measuring.
steps: a and b form a linear pair, so b = 180 − 120 = 60.
b and c form a linear pair, so c = 180 − 60 = 120.
c and d form a linear pair, so d = 180 − 120 = 60.
So a and c are 120°, and b and d are 60°.

source: Two lines cross and a = 35°. Use linear pairs to find b and

items.question: Two lines cross and a = 35°. Use linear pairs to find b and d, then show that they are equal for any value of a.
steps: a and b form a linear pair, so b = 180 − 35 = 145.
a and d form a linear pair, so d = 180 − 35 = 145.
For any a: b = 180 − a and d = 180 − a, so b and d are equal whatever a is.
In the same way, c = 180 − b = a, so a and c are equal. This justification is a proof.
items.answer: b = 145° and d = 145°; vertically opposite angles are always equal

videos.answer: b = 145° and d = 145°; vertically opposite angles are always equal

source: Figure it Out (intersecting lines), Q1

items.question: Two lines l and m cross, and the four angles are named a, b, c and d going round the crossing, with a and b neighbours. List all the linear pairs and all the pairs of vertically opposite angles.
steps: Linear pairs are neighbouring angles that sit on a straight line: a and b, b and c, c and d, d and a.
Vertically opposite angles face each other across the crossing: a and c, b and d.
Check: going round, there are four neighbouring pairs and two facing pairs.
items.answer: Linear pairs: a and b, b and c, c and d, d and a. Vertically opposite pairs: a and c, b and d

videos.answer: Linear pairs: a and b, b and c, c and d, d and a. Vertically opposite pairs: a and c, b and d

source: Imran measures a linear pair as 63° and 119°. Their sum is n

items.question: Imran measures a linear pair as 63° and 119°. Their sum is not 180°. Does that break the rule? What should the second angle be?
steps: 63 + 119 = 182, which is 2° more than 180.
The rule of 180° comes from a straight line with no thickness; a drawn line is thick and the reading of a protractor can be off by a degree or two.
By reasoning, the second angle is 180 − 63 = 117.
So the measure 119° is 2° off, a measurement error, and the rule is not broken.
items.answer: No; the second angle should be 117°, and the 2° is a measurement error

videos.answer: No; the second angle should be 117°, and the 2° is a measurement error

source: Two lines cross so that all four angles are equal. Find each

items.question: Two lines cross so that all four angles are equal. Find each angle, and say what the lines are called.
steps: Two neighbouring angles are a linear pair, so together they are 180°.
They are equal, so each is 180 ÷ 2 = 90.
All four angles are 90°, that is, right angles.
Lines that intersect at right angles are perpendicular, however the pair is tilted.
items.answer: Each angle is 90°, and the lines are perpendicular

videos.answer: Each angle is 90°, and the lines are perpendicular

source: Five pairs of segments are drawn. FG and FH share the end F,

items.question: Five pairs of segments are drawn. FG and FH share the end F, with 115.3° between them. AB and CD cross at X, at about 60°, a little past the middle of each. IJ and LM cross at Y, at about 80°, close to the middle of both. Describe each pair in mathematical words.
steps: FG and FH meet at the endpoint F, at an angle of 115.3°.
AB and CD intersect at the point X, at an angle of about 60°. X is not the midpoint of either segment.
IJ and LM intersect at the point Y, at an angle of about 80°. Y is close to the midpoint of both segments.
The 60° and 80° are measured, so they are close values, as the earlier topic explained.
items.answer: FG and FH meet at the endpoint F at 115.3°; AB and CD intersect at X at about 60°; IJ and LM intersect close to both midpoints at about 80°

videos.answer: FG and FH meet at the endpoint F at 115.3°; AB and CD intersect at X at about 60°; IJ and LM intersect close to both midpoints at about 80°

source: Two more pairs are drawn: ST and UV lean towards each other

items.question: Two more pairs are drawn: ST and UV lean towards each other by about 2.5° and look nearly side by side; OP and QR keep about the same gap along their whole length. Are ST and UV likely to meet if extended? Are OP and QR?
steps: ST and UV lean towards each other, so far beyond T and V they would meet, about four lengths of the segment beyond the ends.
OP and QR keep the same gap from one end to the other, so they are not likely to meet.
By eye we can only guess for lines this close, so we will need a sure test.
items.answer: ST and UV would meet if extended far enough; OP and QR are not likely to meet

videos.answer: ST and UV would meet if extended far enough; OP and QR are not likely to meet

source: Nine segments a to i are drawn on a grid. a, h and i are upr

items.question: Nine segments a to i are drawn on a grid. a, h and i are upright. c and g are flat. d and f lean one way, each along the diagonal of a square. b and e lean the other way, also along the diagonal of a square. Which pairs of lines appear to be parallel?
steps: Upright segments: a, h and i keep the same gap, so they appear parallel to each other.
Flat segments: c and g appear parallel to each other.
Segments leaning one way: d and f appear parallel to each other.
Segments leaning the other way: b and e appear parallel to each other.
A flat segment and an upright one cross; they are not parallel.
items.answer: a, h and i; c and g; d and f; b and e

videos.answer: a, h and i; c and g; d and f; b and e

source: A square sheet has two flat edges. Fold it horizontally in h

items.question: A square sheet has two flat edges. Fold it horizontally in half again and again. Count the parallel lines, including the two edges, after one, two, three and four folds. What is the pattern?
steps: Opposite edges are parallel, and adjacent edges are perpendicular.
After 1 fold there are 2 gaps, so 2 + 1 = 3 parallel lines.
After 2 folds there are 4 gaps, so 4 + 1 = 5 parallel lines.
After 3 folds there are 8 gaps, so 8 + 1 = 9 parallel lines.
After 4 folds there are 16 gaps, so 16 + 1 = 17 parallel lines.
Every fold doubles the gaps, so the number of lines is 1 more than the gaps, 3, 5, 9, 17, ...
items.answer: 3, 5, 9 and 17 parallel lines; the gaps double and the lines are one more than the gaps

videos.answer: 3, 5, 9 and 17 parallel lines; the gaps double and the lines are one more than the gaps

source: Fold a square sheet along one diagonal. Describe a fold that

items.question: Fold a square sheet along one diagonal. Describe a fold that makes a line parallel to this diagonal and say why it is parallel.
steps: Fold the corner that is not on the diagonal onto the centre of the sheet.
The crease is at right angles to the other diagonal, because the fold sends the corner straight along it to the centre.
The first diagonal is also at right angles to the other diagonal.
Two lines at right angles to the same line are parallel, so the crease is parallel to the diagonal.
items.answer: Fold a corner onto the centre; the crease is parallel to the diagonal

videos.answer: Fold a corner onto the centre; the crease is parallel to the diagonal

source: A square sheet is folded in the middle both ways, the edges

items.question: A square sheet is folded in the middle both ways, the edges are folded to the centre line, and then two opposite corners are folded onto a centre crease to make triangles. Pairs of creases a and p, b and q, c and r are marked. Are they parallel?
steps: a and p lie along folds that run the same way, so they lie on parallel lines.
b and q are both perpendicular to those lines, so b and q are parallel to each other.
c and r are the slanting edges of the two folded triangles. Both triangular folds are made against the same diagonal direction, so c and r are parallel.
So a is parallel to p, b to q, and c to r.
items.answer: Yes: a is parallel to p, b to q and c to r

videos.answer: Yes: a is parallel to p, b to q and c to r

source: A drawing has two flat parallel lines, two slanting parallel

items.question: A drawing has two flat parallel lines, two slanting parallel lines, and one upright line that crosses a flat line at 90°. How are these marked?
steps: The flat parallel lines are the first set: one arrow mark on each.
The slanting parallel lines are the second set: two arrow marks on each.
The upright line and the flat line are perpendicular: a small square in the corner between them.
The 90° is not written out; the square says it.
items.answer: One arrow on each flat line, two arrows on each slanting line, and a square at the right angle

videos.answer: One arrow on each flat line, two arrows on each slanting line, and a square at the right angle

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q1

items.question: Draw some lines perpendicular to the lines given on the dot paper. There are two grids, each 3 dots across and 4 dots up. In the left grid, one segment is flat, 2 steps long, and another leans with 2 steps across and 2 steps up. In the right grid, one segment has 2 steps across and 3 steps down, and another is upright, 2 steps long.
steps: Flat segment: an upright segment is perpendicular to it, so draw upright segments between dots (0 steps across, some steps up).
Leaning segment with 2 across and 2 up: swap the steps and change one sign, giving 2 across and 2 down. Draw leaning segments of 2 across and 2 down.
Upright segment: a flat segment is perpendicular to it, so draw flat segments between dots.

Segment with 2 across and 3 down: the perpendicular needs 3 across and 2 up, and the grid is only 3 dots, that is 2 steps, across. It cannot be drawn between dots on this grid, so it needs a wider grid or a set square.
Perpendicular lines need not be one flat and one upright: the leaning ones also meet at 90°.
items.answer: Upright lines for the flat segment, flat lines for the upright one, lines of 2 across and 2 down for the leaning one; the 2-across-3-down segment needs a wider grid

videos.answer: Upright lines for the flat segment, flat lines for the upright one, lines of 2 across and 2 down for the leaning one; the 2-across-3-down segment needs a wider grid

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q2

items.question: Five shapes are drawn on a dot grid. Each corner is given as (across, down) from the top left. Shape 1: (0,0), (2,2), (2,4), (3,5), (0,5). Shape 2: (6,1), (10,1), (8,3), (4,3). Shape 3: (5,4), (7,6), (7,8), (5,8), (3,6), (5,6). Shape 4: (0,7), (3,7), (0,10). Shape 5: (5,9), (8,9), (11,7), (11,11), (5,11). Mark the parallel lines with arrow marks (a single arrow, double arrow and so on) and the angle between perpendicular lines with a square. (a) How did you spot the perpendicular lines? (b) How did you spot the parallel lines?
steps: Shape 1: the side (0,0) to (2,2) and the side (2,4) to (3,5) both go 1 across and 1 down in each step, so they are parallel (single arrow). The upright sides (2,2) to (2,4) and (0,5) to (0,0) are parallel (double arrow). One right angle, at (0,5), between the upright side and the flat bottom.
Shape 2: (6,1) to (10,1) and (8,3) to (4,3) are both flat, so parallel (single arrow). (10,1) to (8,3) and (4,3) to (6,1) both go 2 across and 2 down, so parallel (double arrow). No right angle.

Shape 3: three pairs. (5,4) to (7,6) with (5,8) to (3,6) (single arrow). (7,6) to (7,8) with (5,6) to (5,4) (double arrow). (7,8) to (5,8) with (3,6) to (5,6) (triple arrow). Right angles at (7,8) and at (5,6).
Shape 4: only one right angle, at (0,7), between the flat side and the upright side. No pair of parallel sides.

Shape 5: (5,9) to (8,9) with (11,11) to (5,11) are flat, parallel (single arrow). (11,7) to (11,11) with (5,11) to (5,9) are upright, parallel (double arrow). Right angles at (5,9), (5,11) and (11,11).
(a) Perpendicular lines: a flat line and an upright line on the grid meet at a right angle.
(b) Parallel lines: segments that repeat the same steps across and down, so the gap between them stays the same.
items.answer: Shape 1: two pairs parallel and one right angle; shape 2: two pairs; shape 3: three pairs and two right angles; shape 4: one right angle; shape 5: two pairs and three right angles. (a) Flat and upright lines meet at 90°. (b) Same steps, same gap

videos.answer: Shape 1: two pairs parallel and one right angle; shape 2: two pairs; shape 3: three pairs and two right angles; shape 4: one right angle; shape 5: two pairs and three right angles. (a) Flat and upright lines meet at 90°. (b) Same steps, same gap

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q3

items.question: On dot paper, draw different sets of parallel lines. The line segments can be of different lengths but should have dots as endpoints.
steps: Flat sets: draw two or three flat segments in different rows; they can have different lengths.
Upright sets: draw two or three upright segments in different columns.
Leaning sets: start at different dots and take the same steps, for example 1 across and 1 up, or 2 across and 1 up, each time.
Check each set: the steps are the same, so the lines keep the same gap and are parallel.
items.answer: Sets of flat lines, upright lines and leaning lines that repeat the same steps, such as 1 across and 1 up, or 2 across and 1 up

videos.answer: Sets of flat lines, upright lines and leaning lines that repeat the same steps, such as 1 across and 1 up, or 2 across and 1 up

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q4

items.question: Using your sense of how parallel lines look, draw lines parallel to the line segments a to h on dot paper (13 dots by 13 dots). Taking steps across to the right and then up or down: a is 1 across, 1 down; b is 2 across, 2 down; c is 3 across, 3 up; d is 4 across, 4 up; e is 1 across, 3 down; f is 1 across, 6 down; g is 5 across, 2 up; h is 10 across, 3 down. (a) Did you find it challenging to draw some of them? (b) Which ones? (c) How did you do it?
steps: a, b, c and d lean at the diagonal of a square, so they are easy to copy by eye.
e, f, g and h have unusual steps, so they are harder to draw by eye.

Method: count the steps across and up of the given segment, start at a new dot, and take the same steps. For e: 1 across and 3 down; for f: 1 across and 6 down; for g: 5 across and 2 up; for h: 10 across and 3 down.
Because the steps are the same, the new segment keeps the same gap and is parallel.
items.answer: (a) Yes. (b) The segments e, f, g and h. (c) Count the steps across and up and repeat them from another dot

videos.answer: (a) Yes. (b) The segments e, f, g and h. (c) Count the steps across and up and repeat them from another dot

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q5

items.question: Which line is parallel to line a, line b or line c? How do you decide this? Line a, line b and line c lean to the right. A steep line meets a at one end and b and c at its other end. The angles the steep line makes are about 30° with a, about 29° with c and about 33° with b.
steps: Compare the angles the steep line makes: with a it is about 30°, with c about 29°, with b about 33°.
The angle with c is close to the angle with a; the angle with b is 3° more.
Equal corresponding angles mean parallel, so c is the line parallel to a.
Another way to see it: c stays the same gap from a, while b closes in.
items.answer: Line c is parallel to line a, because the angles made with the steep line are about equal, 30° and 29°

videos.answer: Line c is parallel to line a, because the angles made with the steep line are about equal, 30° and 29°

source: A transversal t crosses lines l and m. The angles are number

items.question: A transversal t crosses lines l and m. The angles are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 going round the crossing with l, and 5, 6, 7, 8 going round the crossing with m in the same way, so that 1 and 3, 2 and 4, 5 and 7, 6 and 8 are vertically opposite. Can all eight angles have different measures? Can the five angles 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2 be all different?
steps: Vertically opposite angles are equal: angle 1 equals angle 3, 2 equals 4, 5 equals 7 and 6 equals 8.
There are four pairs, so there are at most 4 different measures, and all eight cannot differ.
Among the five angles 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2, the angles 2 and 4 are a vertically opposite pair, so they are equal.
So these five angles cannot all be different.
items.answer: No: at most four different measures; and 2 and 4 are equal, so the five cannot all be different

videos.answer: No: at most four different measures; and 2 and 4 are equal, so the five cannot all be different

source: In the transversal figure, 1, 2, 3, 4 are at the crossing wi

items.question: In the transversal figure, 1, 2, 3, 4 are at the crossing with l and 5, 6, 7, 8 at the crossing with m, with 1 and 5 in the same corner. Name the corresponding angle of each of 2, 3 and 4.
steps: The corresponding angle is in the same corner at the other crossing.
2 is in the same corner as 6, so 2 and 6 are corresponding.
3 is in the same corner as 7, so 3 and 7 are corresponding.
4 is in the same corner as 8, so 4 and 8 are corresponding.
items.answer: 2 and 6, 3 and 7, 4 and 8

videos.answer: 2 and 6, 3 and 7, 4 and 8

source: A line l and a transversal t meet at X, and the angle a betw

items.question: A line l and a transversal t meet at X, and the angle a between them is 60°. Describe how to draw a line m through a point Y on t that is parallel to l, and name the angles that are equal.
steps: The other angle of the linear pair at X is 180 − 60 = 120, so there are two distinct angles, 60° and 120°.
Mark a point Y on t.
Draw a line m through Y that makes a 60° angle with t, on the same side as a, by copying a on tracing paper or with a protractor.
The angle b at Y is 60° and a at X is 60°; they are corresponding angles, and they are equal.
So l and m are parallel.
items.answer: m is parallel to l, since the corresponding angles a and b are both 60°

videos.answer: m is parallel to l, since the corresponding angles a and b are both 60°

source: Lines l and m are parallel, with arrow marks, and t crosses

items.question: Lines l and m are parallel, with arrow marks, and t crosses both. The angle a at l is 65°, and b is its corresponding angle at m. Find b and the other three pairs of corresponding angles.
steps: a and b are corresponding angles of parallel lines, so b = 65°.
The angle next to a on the straight line is 180 − 65 = 115, and its corresponding angle is also 115°.
So of the four pairs of corresponding angles, two pairs are 65° and two pairs are 115°.
Each pair is equal, because the lines are parallel.
items.answer: b = 65°; the four pairs of corresponding angles are 65°, 65°, 115° and 115°

videos.answer: b = 65°; the four pairs of corresponding angles are 65°, 65°, 115° and 115°

source: Two lines l and m lean 10° apart, so they are not parallel.

items.question: Two lines l and m lean 10° apart, so they are not parallel. A transversal t makes 30° with l, and m leans 10° more towards t than l does, so t makes 20° with m on the matching side. Can the two corresponding angles be made equal by turning t?
steps: The corresponding angles are 30° and 20°, and 30 − 20 = 10.
Turn t to make 50° with l; then it makes 40° with m, and 50 − 40 = 10.
Each time the two angles differ by 10°, because the lines lean 10° apart.
So no transversal makes them equal: corresponding angles of lines that are not parallel are never equal.
items.answer: No; the corresponding angles always differ by 10°

videos.answer: No; the corresponding angles always differ by 10°

source: Draw a line l with a ruler. Slide a set square along l and d

items.question: Draw a line l with a ruler. Slide a set square along l and draw two lines along its upright edge. Are the two lines parallel? Which angles prove it?
steps: The upright edge of the set square makes a 90° angle with l each time it is drawn.
Seen with l as the transversal, the two angles of 90° are corresponding angles.
The corresponding angles are equal, both 90°.
So the two lines are parallel.
items.answer: Yes, parallel: the corresponding angles are both 90°

videos.answer: Yes, parallel: the corresponding angles are both 90°

source: Place the long side of a 45° set square so that it makes 45°

items.question: Place the long side of a 45° set square so that it makes 45° with l, and draw along it, then slide and draw again. Are the two lines parallel? How can you check?
steps: The long side makes 45° with l each time, because the set square does not turn.
The two angles of 45° are corresponding angles of the transversal l.
They are equal, so the lines are parallel.
To check, trace one angle and slide the tracing over the other, or measure both with a protractor.
items.answer: Yes, parallel: the corresponding angles are both 45°

videos.answer: Yes, parallel: the corresponding angles are both 45°

source: A crease l and a point A are given. Fold a line m through A

items.question: A crease l and a point A are given. Fold a line m through A parallel to l, and say why it is parallel.
steps: Fold the paper so that l falls on itself and the crease passes through A. This crease t is perpendicular to l.
Unfold. Now fold the paper so that t falls on itself and the new crease passes through A. This crease is m, perpendicular to t.
t crosses l at 90° and crosses m at 90°, and these are corresponding angles.
The corresponding angles are equal, so l and m are parallel.
items.answer: m is parallel to l, since both are perpendicular to t, so the corresponding angles are both 90°

videos.answer: m is parallel to l, since both are perpendicular to t, so the corresponding angles are both 90°

source: Figure it Out (drawing parallel lines), Q1

items.question: Can you draw a line parallel to l that goes through the point A? How will you do it with the tools from your geometry box? Describe your method.
steps: You need a ruler, a set square, a pencil and an eraser.
Place the set square so that one side lies along l.
Hold the ruler against another side of the set square, so that the ruler will not move.
Slide the set square along the ruler until the side that was along l reaches the point A.
Draw a line along that side, through A.
This line is parallel to l: the set square did not turn, so it made the same angle with the ruler, and the corresponding angles are equal.
items.answer: Slide the set square along a ruler until its side reaches A and draw along it; the line through A is parallel to l

videos.answer: Slide the set square along a ruler until its side reaches A and draw along it; the line through A is parallel to l

source: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angle

items.question: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angles a, b, d, c are at the upper crossing (a top left, b top right, d bottom left, c bottom right), and e, f, h, g are in the same corners at the lower crossing. If f is 120°, find its alternate angle d.
steps: First move: b is the corresponding angle of f, so b = 120°.
Second move: d is the vertically opposite angle of b, so d = 120°.
So f = d = 120°, whatever the size of f.
Alternate angles are equal when the lines are parallel.
items.answer: d = 120°, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal

videos.answer: d = 120°, so alternate angles of parallel lines are equal

source: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angle

items.question: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angles 1, 2, 3, 4 go round the crossing with l and 5, 6, 7, 8 round the crossing with m in the same corners, so 2 and 6 correspond, and 6 and 8 are vertically opposite, and 5 and 6 are a linear pair. If angle 6 is 135°, find the other angles.
steps: Angle 2 is the corresponding angle of 6, so angle 2 is 135°.
Angle 8 is vertically opposite to 6, so it is 135°; angle 4 is the corresponding angle of 8, so it is 135°.
So angles 2, 4, 6 and 8 are all 135°.
Angles 5 and 6 are a linear pair, so angle 5 is 180 − 135 = 45.
In the same way angles 1, 3 and 7 are 45°.
items.answer: Angles 2, 4, 6 and 8 are 135°; angles 1, 3, 5 and 7 are 45°

videos.answer: Angles 2, 4, 6 and 8 are 135°; angles 1, 3, 5 and 7 are 45°

source: Lines l and m are cut by a transversal t, with the angles a,

items.question: Lines l and m are cut by a transversal t, with the angles a, b, d, c at the upper crossing and e, f, h, g in the same corners at the lower crossing. The angle a is 120° and the angle f is 70°. Are l and m parallel?
steps: a and b are a linear pair, so b = 180 − 120 = 60.
b and f are corresponding angles. If l and m were parallel, b would be equal to f.
But b = 60° and f = 70°, which are not equal, as 70 − 60 = 10.
So l and m are not parallel.
items.answer: No: the corresponding angles are 60° and 70°, which are not equal

videos.answer: No: the corresponding angles are 60° and 70°, which are not equal

source: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angle

items.question: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angles 1, 2, 3, 4 go round the crossing with l and 5, 6, 7, 8 round the crossing with m in the same corners, with 2 and 6 corresponding and 2 and 3 a linear pair. If angle 3 is 50°, find angle 6, and say what relation angles 3 and 6 have.
steps: Angles 2 and 3 are a linear pair, so angle 2 is 180 − 50 = 130.
Angles 2 and 6 are corresponding angles of parallel lines, so angle 6 is 130°.
Angles 3 and 6 are interior angles on the same side, and 50 + 130 = 180.
This holds for any angle 3: angle 3 and angle 2 add to 180, and angle 2 equals angle 6, so angle 3 and angle 6 add to 180.
items.answer: Angle 6 = 130°; interior angles on the same side add to 180°

videos.answer: Angle 6 = 130°; interior angles on the same side add to 180°

source: A four-sided figure ABCD has AB parallel to CD and AD parall

items.question: A four-sided figure ABCD has AB parallel to CD and AD parallel to BC, and a line from A to C inside it. Angle DAC is 65° and angle ADC is 60°. Find angles DAB, CAB, BCD and ABC.
steps: AB is parallel to CD and AD is a transversal, so angle ADC + angle DAB = 180°.
Angle DAB = angle DAC + angle CAB, so 120 = 65 + CAB, and angle CAB = 120 − 65 = 55°.
AD is parallel to BC and CD is a transversal, so angle ADC + angle BCD = 180°, and angle BCD = 180 − 60 = 120°.
In the same way, angle ABC = 60°.
items.answer: Angle DAB = 120°, angle CAB = 55°, angle BCD = 120°, angle ABC = 60°

videos.answer: Angle DAB = 120°, angle CAB = 55°, angle BCD = 120°, angle ABC = 60°

source: Figure it Out (angles), Q1

items.question: Find the angles marked below. In every figure two or three lines are parallel and a transversal crosses them. (a) An angle of 48° and a are corresponding angles. (b) An angle of 52° and b are alternate angles. (c) An angle of 99° is shown, and c is its interior partner on the same side. (d) An angle of 81° is shown, and d is its interior partner on the same side. (e) Angles of 97°, 83° and 69° are shown, and e is the alternate angle of the 69°. (f) An angle of 132° is shown, and f is its interior partner on the same side. (g) Angles of 58° and 122° are shown on the right line, and g is the angle in the matching lower left corner at the left line, corresponding to the 122°. (h) Angles of 75° and 120° are shown, and h is the alternate angle of the 75°. (i) Between two slanted parallel lines, the angles 54°, 70° and 56° lie along one straight line, and i is the alternate angle of the 54° across the steep line. (j) Three parallel lines are crossed by a line, with angles of 27°, 97° and 124° shown; j is the vertically opposite angle of the corresponding angle of the 97°.
steps: (a) Corresponding angles of parallel lines are equal, so a = 48.
(b) Alternate angles of parallel lines are equal, so b = 52.
(c) Interior angles on the same side add to 180, so c = 180 − 99 = 81.
(d) In the same way, d = 180 − 81 = 99.
(e) Alternate angles are equal, so e = 69. The 97° and 83° are not needed.
(f) Interior angles on the same side add to 180, so f = 180 − 132 = 48.
(g) The 122° and 58° form a linear pair, 122 + 58 = 180, and g corresponds to the 122°, so g = 122.
(h) Alternate angles are equal, so h = 75. The 120° is not needed.
(i) Alternate angles are equal, so i = 54. The 70° and 56° are not needed, but they fit with i on a straight line: 54 + 70 + 56 = 180.
(j) The corresponding angle of 97° is 97°, and its vertically opposite angle is 97°, so j = 97. The 27° and 124° are not needed.

source: Figure it Out (angles), Q2

items.question: Find the angle represented by a in each figure. (i) Two parallel lines with an angle of 42°; a is its interior partner on the same side; a separate angle of 100° is shown but not needed. (ii) Two parallel lines with an angle of 62°; a is the other angle of the linear pair of the corresponding angle of the 62°. (iii) An angle of 110° contains an angle of 35°; the rest of the 110° is the corresponding angle of the angle that makes a linear pair with a. (iv) An angle of 67° and a make a right angle between a transversal and a line perpendicular to the parallels.
steps: (i) Interior angles on the same side add to 180, so a = 180 − 42 = 138. The 100° is not needed.
(ii) The corresponding angle of the 62° is 62°, and a is a linear pair of it, so a = 180 − 62 = 118.
(iii) The rest of the 110° is 110 − 35 = 75, which is the corresponding angle next to a on a straight line, so a = 180 − 75 = 105.
(iv) The 67° and a fill a right angle, so a = 90 − 67 = 23.

source: Figure it Out (angles), Q3

items.question: In the figures, what angles do x and y stand for? (i) Two parallel lines and a transversal: a right angle is split into 65° and x, and y makes a linear pair with x. (ii) Two lines cross above a lower line; the lower line makes 78° with one of them and 53° with the other, and x is the angle between the two upper lines.
steps: (i) x and 65° fill a right angle, so x = 90 − 65 = 25.
(i) y and x form a linear pair, so y = 180 − 25 = 155.
(ii) The two lines make angles of 78° and 53° with the lower line, so the angle between them is the difference: x = 78 − 53 = 25.

source: Figure it Out (angles), Q4

items.question: Angle ABC is 45° and angle IKJ is 78°. The points D, E and G lie on a straight line, and the rays EH and EF go up from E on one side, in the order G, H, F, D. The sides of angle GEH are parallel to the sides of angle ABC, and the sides of angle FED are parallel to the sides of angle IKJ. Find angle GEH, angle HEF and angle FED.
steps: Angle GEH is the corresponding angle of angle ABC, and then its vertically opposite angle, so angle GEH = 45°.
Angle FED corresponds to angle IKJ in the same way, so angle FED = 78°.
G, E and D lie on a straight line, so the three angles GEH, HEF and FED add to 180°.
items.answer: Angle GEH = 45°, angle HEF = 57°, angle FED = 78°

videos.answer: Angle GEH = 45°, angle HEF = 57°, angle FED = 78°

items.question: AB is parallel to CD, and CD is parallel to EF. Also, EA is perpendicular to AB. The angle BEF is 55°. Here x is the angle at B between BE and the part of AB going down from B, and y is the angle that corresponds to x where BE crosses CD. Find the values of x and y.
steps: AB and EF are parallel and BE is a transversal. The angle x at B and the angle BEF at E are interior angles on the same side, so they add to 180°.
y is the corresponding angle of x where BE crosses the parallel line CD, so y = 125.
The perpendicular EA is not needed for the values of x and y.

items.question: What is the measure of angle NOP? The lines LM and PQ are parallel. At M the angle between ML and MN is 40°, at N the angle between NM and NO is 96°, and at P the angle between PO and PQ is 52°. Hint: draw lines parallel to LM and PQ through the points N and O.
steps: Draw a line through N and a line through O, both parallel to LM and PQ.
The line through N makes 40° with NM, an alternate angle of the 40° at M. The rest of the 96° at N is 96 − 40 = 56, between that line and NO.
The two new lines are parallel, so the angle at O between ON and the line through O is also 56°, an alternate angle. The angle between OP and that line is 52°, an alternate angle of the 52° at P.
Angle NOP is that 56° together with the 52°.
items.answer: Angle NOP = 108°

videos.answer: Angle NOP = 108°

source: In a picture, two upright lines run through a burst of spoke

items.question: In a picture, two upright lines run through a burst of spokes, and they seem to bend outwards in the middle. How can we check whether they are parallel? What causes the illusion?
steps: Lay a ruler along each line: it fits the whole line, so each line is straight.
Measure the gap between the two lines at the top, the middle and the bottom: it is the same each time, so the lines are parallel.
The spokes cut the lines at many different angles, and the eye misjudges the angles, so the lines seem to bend.
A measurement and a reason can overrule what the eye seems to see.
items.answer: The lines are straight and parallel; the crossing spokes trick the eye about angles

videos.answer: The lines are straight and parallel; the crossing spokes trick the eye about angles
